To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a higher dietary protein intake improves weight maintenance after a weight loss in overweight subjects.

the additional protein intake of 30 g/d in overweight subjects after very-low-energy diet resulted in improved weight maintenance, improved body composition and fat distribution, improved substrate oxidation, and improved satiety.

additional protein intake of 30 g/d during a 6-month weight maintenance period after a very-low-energy weight loss diet limited weight regain, improved body composition and fat distribution, improved satiety and substrate oxidation and improved weight maintenance after a 6-month follow-up period.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the importance of protein intake for long-term weight management in overweight individuals.
the effects of protein intake on weight regain after a short-term weight loss.
a new strategy for weight maintenance, which is to add protein to the diet.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
protein intake of at least 18 % of total energy intake limits weight regain and improves body composition after weight loss in overweight subjects.
a higher protein intake during WM after weight loss is beneficial.

a protein intake of 30 % of energy intake during a 6-month follow-up period after a very-low-energy-diet period of 4 weeks is more effective in limiting weight regain than the usual protein intake of 15 %.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
protein intake of 30 g/d on top of the habitual diet improves WM after weight loss.
a high protein intake during weight maintenance may be an effective strategy to prevent weight regain after weight reduction.
protein intake of 1·2 g/kg body weight/d during WM is a promising approach to limit weight regain in humans.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a protein intake of 1·5 g/kg per d is sufficient to limit weight regain.
the addition of protein can be a useful tool to limit weight regain after weight reduction in humans.
protein supplementation is an easy and cheap intervention that may improve long-term WM in overweight subjects.
